rationale: A clean, internally consistent measurement correction (since Compustat's oibdp is net of xrd via xsga, the add-back is arithmetically valid) that directly tests whether the gen-6 breakthrough is an expensing artefact rather than a two-anomaly blend, though it edges toward the well-documented intangible-adjusted-profitability literature.

Economically coherent and diagnostically useful, but it is only a funding-leg swap between two legs already extensively tested in the archive, so it is a recombination rather than a new construct and its incremental information is limited to which quality dimension dominates.

Replacing the R&D flow with a five-year knowledge stock is a defensible and standard refinement (close to the known R&D-capital anomaly), but the stated justification is internally wrong — scaling the stock by `at` creates a shared denominator with the oibdp/at profitability leg rather than breaking one — and undepreciated cumulative spend mostly re-ranks the same firms as current intensity.

The test cannot discriminate what it claims, because xsga in Compustat generally subsumes xrd (so the SG&A leg partly reproduces the R&D leg mechanically) while simultaneously suffering the exact cancellation problem the author criticised in the parent — oibdp is computed net of xsga, so ranking profitability and SG&A intensity together offsets — and organisation-capital-from-SG&A is itself a published anomaly.

A legitimate and well-motivated sector-bet diagnostic for a leg known to be heavily industry-clustered, but it is a robustness variant of the parent rather than a new mechanism, and its main value is confirmatory rather than exploratory.

The intangible-adjusted return-on-financed-capital numerator is a genuinely new measurement construct, but the proposal changes three things at once relative to the breakthrough (R&D add-back, invested-capital denominator, and a swap of the funding leg from debt maturity to working capital), so any result will be uninterpretable as to which change drove it.
